metadata.title: Noah Shinn — Building Instinct: The Personal Agent

conclusion: Shinn is shipping a personal agent that already transacts — text, call, email, no new app. Invite-only, five invites, $0 of marketing, and 10–11% day-over-day from a 200-person start; eBay listed invites at $300. Volume is already over $1B a year on a tiny base, half of it travel. Three weeks in, 40% have handed over a card and one sensitive share prints about 80% retention. The raise is about $1B at roughly $10B with Sequoia, Benchmark, and Coatue. Compute needed doubles about every week. He wants a merchant take-rate, not ads.
background: First long-form with Noah Shinn on Instinct, the year-old personal assistant. Patrick wants what it already does (US Open tape, wardrobe shopping, cancelled subscriptions), the trusted-person network, why the product is free, and how a tiny company buys compute that doubles every week against Meta, Apple, and Amazon. Topics: take-rates, Muse, safety firewalls, and voice-first use.
important_facts: Product and proof: Instinct is about a year old. No new app — it has a phone and a computer, so you text, call, or email it (Patrick has had about three calls). It fetched US Open jumbotron footage. Shoppers scan a wardrobe and get thousands of outfits rendered on their own body; some ask for three new looks a day. It cancels unused subscriptions and has come back with $2,000 this month saved. The trusted-person network is about 10 days old: two Instincts book a meeting; a six-person group had one Uber pick everyone up. Invite-only, five invites, started at 200 friends and is now 10–11% day-over-day with $0 of marketing. Invites sold on eBay for $300. Annualized volume is already over $1B on a tiny base; 50% is travel. Three weeks in, 40% have shared a card; one sensitive share prints about 80% retention.

Money and incumbents: he will not run ads. Google, TikTok, Instagram, and Snapchat are the free-to-user, paid-to-influence model he refuses if the agent is smarter than the person. Volume is compounding at about 10% a day. He wants a merchant take-rate like Apple Pay: user free, merchant pays. A digital payment already has about 40 parties sharing 2–2.5%. Shopify takes about 2–3%, Amazon upwards of 10%, Apple in-app 30%. Boutique hotels will pay up to 30% for a booked room; half of volume is travel. Attention businesses get cut; ride or meal volume can rise if checkout is zero-friction — a car always waiting because Instinct has the calendar. More than 50% of traffic is not on iMessage.

Compute and trust: the window versus the biggest players is months. He spends about 40% of his time on compute. 10% day-over-day doubles demand about every week; buy 2x and it is gone in a week, buy 10x and it is gone in a couple of weeks, and new clusters have a multi-month lead time (wrong by 3–4x if you miss). Even 5–8% for three to four months is 100 million users. They match Opus 5 engagement on cheaper batch shapes (3x to 8x more efficient). Goal is free for a lifetime, not a $100/month subscription. Early product lacked inbound firewalls and a decoupled action monitor; those now sit off the agent. Some users send more than 90% of messages by voice. Latest round is about $1B at roughly a $10B valuation, with Sequoia, Benchmark, and Coatue.

mental_model.name: No App × Trust Ramp × Merchant Take-Rate
mental_model.components: Meet people in text, call, and email, not a new icon. Capability is a computer plus a phone; the product job is understandability and feel, which is why word of mouth hit 10–11% day-over-day with five invites and no spend. Trust is a three-week ramp: 40% share a card, one sensitive share prints ~80% retention. Keep the user in control of data. Money is a take-rate on merchants (Apple Pay shape), not ads that steer a smarter agent against the user. Compute is the constraint: demand doubles about weekly and clusters take months, so he buys ahead and customizes inference. Agents talking to agents (trusted network, calendar, Uber route) is the new social graph.
mental_model.application: Private:Instinct is the named vehicle: $1B-plus run-rate volume on a tiny invite base, ~$10B raise, Sequoia/Benchmark/Coatue. AAPL is the take-rate map (Pay free to user; 30% in-app as the top of the curve) and one channel (iMessage), though more than half of traffic is already elsewhere. UBER is the zero-friction ride: if Instinct always has a car because it owns the calendar, trip volume of the underlying service should rise. AMZN sits on his 10% platform-fee mark and the Muse comparison — goods volume can go up, attention/upsell can get cut. Fade attention-only apps. Do not model this as a $100/month seat.

key_insights.question: Is this still a demo?
key_insights.answer: Over $1B a year on a small invite base, half travel. Three-week card share is 40%. eBay was asking $300 for an invite.

key_insights.view: Charge the merchant, never the user.
key_insights.question: How do you stay aligned?
key_insights.answer: Ads would let a smarter agent sell against you. Apple Pay / Amex is the shape; Shopify 2–3%, Amazon ~10%, Apple 30% are the curve.

key_insights.question: What can kill the compounding?
key_insights.answer: Lead times of months at 5–8% day-over-day is 100 million users. He spends ~40% of his time buying ahead. Wrong is 3–4x expensive.

top_investment_implications.thesis: Invite-only 10–11% day-over-day, $1B-plus volume on a tiny base, ~$10B raise; trust ramp is the product — medium
Named ride example: a car always waiting because the agent has the calendar should raise trip volume as checkout friction goes to zero — low
Apple Pay is his free-to-user, merchant-pays model; 30% in-app is the top of the take-rate curve he is mapping — low

golden_quotes: This is probably the most exciting software race ever
we're approaching over a billion dollars a year in transaction volume through the platform
3 weeks in, there's a 40% chance that the user has shared a personal credit card with Instinct.
